blockers.title: Local working tree's main branch has diverged from origin/main and cannot be reconciled by this headless run
blockers.detail: Local HEAD (ee592f61, a 'daily QA run 2026-08-15' commit) is NOT an ancestor of origin/main -- it branched off 75b8f68c (2026-08-14 docs commit) independently of origin's own 08-15 line, which carries de692a85 (a DIFFERENT 08-15 QA commit) plus 1770078c and b6108f26 (blog-batch/deploy commits never received locally) and 697aef80 (08-15 GSC triage). Merge-base is 75b8f68c. This means two independent sessions each committed their own 08-15 QA findings locally, and only one (origin's) made it to the remote. The local tree ALSO carries known, deliberately-uncommitted WIP (destination-detail-cinematic.tsx affiliate-links feature, analytics.ts, env.example -- matches the 'stayPicks.disclosure' WIP documented in CLAUDE.md's commit 677b6854 note) that must not be swept into any commit.
evidence: git status --short shows unrelated modified files (destination-detail-cinematic.tsx, analytics.ts, env.example, several qa/findings/2026-05-04-deep/axe-reports/*.json)
blockers.consequence: Per project memory (git push/lock sandbox gaps), a diverged branch must be reconciled in a throwaway worktree, never the shared tree, and never by an unattended headless run. Committing on top of local HEAD would deepen the divergence; force-pushing would risk losing origin's blog-batch/GSC-triage commits.
blockers.recommendation: Attempted the throwaway-worktree approach (git worktree add from origin/main into /tmp/audit-wt) rather than touching the divergent local tree -- this is the correct approach per project memory, but it could not be completed in this sandbox. See GIT-PUSH-BLOCKED-2026-08-16-002 below for why and what's still needed.

blockers.title: Could NOT commit or push today's QA artifacts to git -- CLAUDE.md's standing rule for headless audit sessions was not satisfiable in this sandbox
blockers.detail: Two independent environment blockers, neither fixable from within this session: (1) No `gh` CLI is installed in this sandbox (`gh: command not found`), and the repo's configured credential.helper is `!gh auth git-credential` -- so any git operation needing push auth (a worktree push, or a fresh `git clone` over HTTPS which also hung waiting on the same credential helper and had to be killed after timing out) has no way to authenticate. Reads (git fetch) work fine without auth, which is why the earlier fetch/comparison against origin/main succeeded. (2) Independently, `git worktree add` itself left stale, empty (0-byte) lock files under .git/worktrees/audit-wt/ on the FUSE-mounted repo path, and this sandbox's FUSE layer refuses to unlink them ('Operation not permitted') even though they are owned by this user with normal 0600 permissions and no process holds them (verified via pgrep) -- a filesystem-level restriction, not a real lock contention. This blocked `git add` inside the worktree entirely, independent of the auth problem.
evidence: `rm -f .git/worktrees/audit-wt/index.lock` => 'Operation not permitted' despite `ls -la` showing 0600 ownership by the current user and 0 live git processes via pgrep
`git clone https://github.com/.../india-travel-planner.git /tmp/audit-clone` hung and was killed after a 120s timeout
blockers.consequence: qa/findings/2026-08-16.json and the qa/findings/2026-08-16/ evidence artifacts exist ONLY in this workspace folder (not on origin/main) as of the end of this run. The 3 .docx reports are gitignored by design (/NakshIQ_*.docx in .gitignore) so their absence from git is normal and expected, not part of this gap. A residual, harmless side-effect: a 'audit-push-2026-08-16' worktree registration + branch is now stuck (locked, unremovable from this sandbox) pointing at /tmp/audit-wt, which will vanish when this session's /tmp clears -- the founder can clean up the dangling registration later with `git worktree remove -f -f /tmp/audit-wt && git branch -D audit-push-2026-08-16` from a machine without this FUSE restriction; it does not affect the main checkout's branch or HEAD.
blockers.recommendation: Founder action needed: either (a) install/authenticate `gh` in future scheduled-task sandboxes so audit-commit-guard.sh can push directly, or (b) manually commit+push qa/findings/2026-08-16.json and qa/findings/2026-08-16/ from a machine with working git credentials, or (c) treat this as a one-off gap -- tomorrow's run will still work from origin/main's current state (today's findings just won't be the 'previous run' baseline for git-history purposes, only for the local findings/*.json file comparison, which is unaffected since that file IS present in this workspace).
